name: monolake
workload: HTTP and HTTPS proxy/serving throughput of the Monolake reference proxy (Rust on the io_uring-based monoio runtime) against nginx, measured as requests per second versus response body size (512 B to 64 KiB) and versus worker threads (1 to 16); load generator, nginx configuration and backend setup are not stated.
claimed_speedup: No numbers in the text; four chart images only. Approximate values read from the charts (not stated by the project). HTTPS vs worker threads: 16 threads about 526k req/s vs nginx about 450k (about 1.17x), 8 threads about 359k vs about 334k (about 1.07x). HTTPS vs body size: 512 B about 152k vs about 128k (about 1.19x), 4096 B about 124k vs about 108k (about 1.15x), roughly equal at 8192 B, then nginx ahead at 16384 B (about 55k vs about 59k) and 65536 B (about 20k vs about 23k). Plain HTTP: nginx ahead everywhere, 16 threads about 707k vs about 688k (monolake about 0.97x), 512 B about 186k vs about 168k (monolake about 0.91x).
compiler_and_flags: Not stated for Monolake or nginx; Monolake needs Rust nightly and Linux 5.1+ for io_uring (docs).
hardware: AWS c6a.8xlarge, AMD EPYC 7R13, 16 cores / 32 threads, 64 GB RAM, Linux 6.1.94-99.176.amzn2023.x86_64 (Amazon Linux 2023.5.20240805), nginx 1.24.0 (README Performance section)
stars_or_usage: 66 stars; README says it was deployed in production at ByteDance
tradeoffs: Archived by the owner on 2025-08-29 and marked no longer recommended for use; needs Rust nightly and Linux io_uring (falls back to epoll elsewhere); HTTP/Thrift proxy framework rather than a general web server.
caveats: First-party charts with no tabulated numbers, so values here are eyeballed from PNGs. The win is confined to HTTPS with small bodies (and more worker threads); plain HTTP and large HTTPS bodies favour nginx. The nginx build and configuration (workers, logging, TLS library), the workload (static body or proxied backend) and the load generator are not stated, and the TLS stack on each side is unknown. Repository is archived. Tier C: first-party, partial methodology.
found_via: WebSearch 'monolake Rust proxy benchmark vs Nginx throughput cloudwego' surfaced the project; github.com/cloudwego/monolake README Performance section and its four chart PNGs (raw.githubusercontent.com .github/images) opened
why_faster: Thread-per-core io_uring runtime (monoio) with no work stealing, versus nginx's epoll workers; the README gives no explicit explanation for the HTTPS win.

name: zix
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG); same suite rows for libreactorng (C, io_uring), libioma (C), h2o (C), mongoose (C), agensio (C++), Drogon (C++) and userver (C++)
workload: HttpArena profiles on the zix.Http1 URING dispatch engine (per-worker SO_REUSEPORT io_uring loops, comptime router): baseline (mixed GET/POST with query parsing, 4096 connections), 16x pipelined, limited-conn, JSON over TLS, JSON over cleartext h2c, h2/h2c/h3 baseline and gzip JSON.
claimed_speedup: baseline-4096: 4,442,329 req/s vs nginx 3,284,513 (1.35x, derived from page data), h2o 3,641,609 (1.22x), mongoose 3,707,598 (1.20x), libioma 4,255,834 (1.04x), libreactorng 4,377,377 (1.01x, within noise), Drogon 2,022,710 (2.20x). pipelined-4096: 58,761,616 vs libreactorng 43,424,448 (1.35x), nginx 4,037,345 (14.6x), Drogon 7,801,404 (7.5x). json-tls-4096: 1,845,248 vs agensio (C++) 1,716,076 (1.08x), nginx 1,313,755 (1.40x). baseline-h3-64: 9,086,240 vs agensio 8,634,941 (1.05x), nginx 4,849,624 (1.87x). json-h2c-4096: 6,746,440 vs agensio 4,108,364 (1.64x), nginx 1,691,740 (4.0x). Not a clean win: baseline-h2-256 14,076,613 vs h2o 16,106,978 (0.87x, h2o ahead) and agensio 14,744,015; static-tls-1024 339,689 vs nginx 720,869 (0.47x, slower); limited-conn-4096 2,708,192 vs libioma 2,707,029 (equal).
compiler_and_flags: zix: Zig 0.16.0, zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl -Dcpu=x86_64_v3+aes+pclmul+adx --release=fast (frameworks/zix/Dockerfile). nginx: custom C module, ./configure --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG'. libreactorng: gcc -O3 -march=native. libioma: gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto. mongoose: gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto. h2o: clang CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native, no LTO. Drogon: handler built with CMake Release against the prebuilt drogonframework/drogon:latest image.
hardware: HttpArena dedicated machine per site/data/current.json: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (64 cores, 128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), CPU governor performance; each entry runs in a container. current.json is undated and may differ from the machine state of the run behind a given results file.
stars_or_usage: 10 stars (GitHub mirror of a Codeberg repository)
tradeoffs: Young Zig 0.16 network library and HTTP engine; the URING dispatch model is Linux-only and needs a recent kernel; the TLS static-file path is slower than nginx; project is pre-1.0.
caveats: The margin over the fastest C entries at baseline-4096 and limited-conn-4096 is about 1% (libreactorng, libioma), which is within run-to-run noise; the clear wins are over nginx, h2o, mongoose and Drogon, and on pipelined, json-tls, h3 and h2c profiles. HttpArena results JSON files are undated, hold one 5 s run per profile with no repeat count stated, and are rerun by the maintainers, so the numbers can move. The C competitor entries (nginx with a custom C handler module, libreactorng, libioma, h2o, mongoose) are minimal hand-written handlers built by the suite maintainers or contributors, not tuned production configurations; the C/C++ rows are compiled with -O3 -march=native (nginx, libreactorng, libioma, mongoose; libioma and mongoose also with LTO) or CMake Release with clang -march=native (h2o), and the Drogon entry compiles only its handler with CMake Release against the prebuilt drogonframework/drogon:latest Docker image (the Drogon library's own flags are not under the suite's control, so Drogon ratios of 2x to 8x here are weaker evidence than the nginx, h2o, libreactorng and libioma ratios). Response sizes differ between entries (bytes per response derived from bandwidth divided by req/s in the same JSON files: nginx 135.4, Drogon 134.4, libreactorng 108.7, libioma 85.8, mongoose 72.5, versus 62.9 for the Zig, Rust and C# entries at baseline-4096), so the minimal-header entries write fewer bytes per request. The pipelined profile (16x batched pipelining) is reference-only in HttpArena's own composite score. README of zix itself only links to HttpArena and gives no numbers.
found_via: Followed HttpArena (MDA2AV/HttpArena) per-entry results from the WebSearch result for 'the-benchmarker/web-frameworks' style suites; frameworks.json lists zix as a Zig engine; site/data/results/zix.json and the C/C++ sibling files opened via raw.githubusercontent.com
why_faster: Per-worker SO_REUSEPORT io_uring loops with a comptime router and staged send sink (HttpArena meta.json and frameworks.json). The fastest C entries use the same thread-per-core io_uring design, so the gain over nginx (epoll) is architecture, not the language.
